# DESIGN:OS Studio (`design-os-studio`)

**Native GPU-accelerated interface design studio in Rust. It opens and writes `.fig` files with no Figma app installed, runs your own coding agent CLI in an Agents panel on the open file, and ships a Model Context Protocol server (`designos-mcp`) so agents can edit a `.fig` headless.** Open a `.fig`, edit it, and write it back, in the Studio window, or without a window through `designos FILE --inspect-json`, `--export-fig`, `--scan-design-system` and `--codegen`, or through `designos-mcp`. Studio draws the canvas on the GPU with `wgpu` (Metal, DirectX 12 or Vulkan). The Agents panel runs Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Antigravity or Gemini CLI as a live session on the open file with your own sign-in, so Studio needs no API key. Work with variables and modes, select matching layers with Multi-Edit (`Q`), and read Dev Mode code in eight languages (CSS, Tailwind, React, SwiftUI, UIKit, Compose, Android XML and HTML). Saving a `.fig` has [known issue #834](https://github.com/jangtrinh/design-os-studio/issues/834).

Why DESIGN:OS · Facts · Quickstart · Watch · Safe Loop · What's new · What it makes · Micro-Interactions · Install · How it works · Commands · Limits & FAQ

--- ## Studio, designed in Studio Studio's own interface is kept as a design system in a Studio file, [`design/studio-ui.designos`](design/studio-ui.designos): foundations, component sets, Studio surfaces and editor screens on six pages. --- ## Why this exists ### Why DESIGN:OS Studio? Browser-based design tools keep your files on a vendor's servers and give coding agents little more than a REST export. **`design-os-studio`** is a local-first studio written in Rust. It reads and writes `.fig` files on your disk, runs your own agent CLI in an Agents panel, and serves the open file to agents through a local MCP server. | Dimension | DESIGN:OS Studio | How to check | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Rendering** | Native Rust canvas: `wgpu` on Metal, DirectX 12 or Vulkan, with a `tiny-skia` CPU renderer for headless captures. It requests no repaint while the view is idle (`FrameKey` frame reuse). | Open a file, leave it still, and read the process CPU time twice with `ps -o time= -p `. | | **Large files** | A spatial index of 2048-unit grid cells (`SceneIndex`) limits work to the viewport, and repeated shapes share one mesh (`GeomCache`). The 336 MB Untitled UI PRO kit opens as one document of 207,601 nodes. | `designos --inspect-json` prints the node count. | | **`.fig` files** | Reads `.fig` containers (`fig-kiwi`, `DEFLATE` or `Zstd`) and writes container version 106, in a ZIP with `meta.json` and `images/`. [Known issue in 0.6.0](https://github.com/jangtrinh/design-os-studio/issues/834): saving a `.fig` drops numbered-list formatting and writes inherited or variable-bound paints on instances as fixed values. | Export a file, then read the version from the `canvas.fig` header (see below). | | **Agents** | The Agents panel starts your own agent CLI (Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Antigravity or Gemini CLI) as a live session on the open file, and keeps a file's sessions across restarts. Each CLI uses its own sign-in, so Studio needs no API key. | `designos-studio --panel agents` | | **MCP server** | `designos-mcp` serves its tools over stdio: see the design, read its design system, write in one step (`designos_apply_batch`) and lint the result (`designos_lint`). | Send `tools/list` to `designos-mcp --workspace `. The tool table below is generated from that list. | | **Variables** | Color, number, string and boolean variables in collections with modes. A frame can pin its own mode per collection, and modes round-trip through `.fig`. Import and export Figma JSON and W3C Design Tokens (DTCG). | `designos --export-variables ` | | **Dev Mode** | Built-in Dev Mode (`Shift+D`) with code in CSS, Tailwind, React, SwiftUI, UIKit, Compose, Android XML and HTML. | `designos --select --codegen react` | | **Privacy and license** | No telemetry. Studio makes these network requests: open-licensed font downloads from the Fontsource API when a file uses fonts you do not have, a public status-page check after an agent provider error, a connection check when you click Retry connection, and a plugin download from GitHub when you install a plugin. The agent CLIs you start use the network under their own terms. Source-available under `PolyForm Shield 1.0.0`. | `git grep -n 'ureq::' -- crates` lists the HTTP calls. The Figma REST client in `designos-fig` is a cargo feature that is off by default. | To read the container version of an exported file, run `unzip -p out.fig canvas.fig | head -c 12 | xxd`. The header starts with `fig-kiwi` and ends with `6a00 0000`, which is 106 in little-endian. > **Where hosted tools win, and it is not close:** real-time multiplayer with live cursors, enterprise cloud administration with SSO and SCIM, and hosted comment notifications by email or Slack. Studio has none of these. If your workflow needs real-time cloud multiplayer without local file ownership, use Figma (paired with our live bridge [`design-os-figma-plugin`](https://jangtrinh.github.io/design-os-figma-plugin/)) or a hosted Penpot instance instead. --- ### Facts Register | Instrument Field | Specification | Verification / Notes | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Repository** | [`jangtrinh/design-os-studio`](https://github.com/jangtrinh/design-os-studio) | Cargo workspace, `crates/designos-*`. Four binaries ship: `designos-studio`, `designos`, `designos-mcp`, `designos-diff` | | **Engine Stack** | Rust + `wgpu` + `tiny-skia` | Metal (verified on macOS) · Direct3D 12 / Vulkan (Windows and Linux, not verified before release) · No Electron | | **Figma Interop** | Reads `.fig`; writes container version 106 | `crates/designos-fig` round-trip tests · more than `6,000` automated tests pass in the macOS CI job · [known issue #834](https://github.com/jangtrinh/design-os-studio/issues/834) | | **Agent Surface** | Agents panel + `designos-mcp` | `Claude Code` · `Codex` · `Grok` · `Antigravity` · `Gemini CLI`, each with its own sign-in | | **Telemetry / Network** | No telemetry | Network use: font downloads from the Fontsource API for fonts a file needs, a status-page check after an agent provider error, a connection check when you click Retry connection, plugin downloads you start from GitHub, and the agent CLIs you start | | **License** | `PolyForm Shield 1.0.0` (source-available) | Release packages: macOS `.dmg` (verified), Windows `.zip`, Linux `.deb` and `.tar.gz` (built, not verified before release) | --- ## Watch Five short films of DESIGN:OS Studio, starting with an agent editing a `.fig` headless, with no Figma app and no display. Writing `.fig` files is still [known issue #834](https://github.com/jangtrinh/design-os-studio/issues/834). Current release is v0.7.17. FREE and source-available (PolyForm Shield).

Writing .fig files is still #834. - [DESIGN:OS Studio v0.7.10: live connectors that follow your screens](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LJQwnIcHIUA) (1:00): Live connectors that follow your screens, filmed on v0.7.10. - [DESIGN:OS Studio 0.7.0 → 0.7.7: masks, style folders, shadow blend modes, Ask for risky only](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4aDiDqNm8a0) (1:00): A recap of 0.7.0 to 0.7.7: masks, style folders, shadow blend modes, and Ask for risky only. - [DESIGN:OS Studio v0.6.0: a FREE Figma alternative for AI #Shorts](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V76BySt9WOs) (0:30): A 30-second recap of v0.6.0, a FREE Figma alternative built for AI. - [DESIGN:OS Studio: open and write .fig files without Figma](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LDzKn-GSwUk) (1:10): Why Studio exists: open and write .fig files without Figma, with a Native Terminal on the open file. More films: the [DESIGN:OS videos hub](https://jangtrinh.github.io/videos/) and the [design:os by Jang](https://www.youtube.com/@designosbyjang) channel. --- ## Quickstart ### 1. Install once Install the agent skill plugin in Claude Code, copy the skill into Codex, download a release package (`.dmg`, `.zip`, `.deb`, `.tar.gz`), or build the four binaries from source: ```bash # Option A: Claude Code plugin marketplace /plugin marketplace add jangtrinh/design-os-studio /plugin install design-os-studio@design-os-studio # Option B: Clone and launch the native Rust/wgpu Studio (or package a .dmg / .zip / .deb) git clone https://github.com/jangtrinh/design-os-studio cd design-os-studio cargo run --release -p designos-app --bin designos-studio ./scripts/build-release.sh --local-host ``` ### 2. First Safe Use & The Practical Loop **First safe use (three bounded, non-destructive steps):** 1. **Run the deterministic offline repository, crate, and skill self-check:** ```bash python3 scripts/self_check.py ``` 2. **Apply `--apply-spec your-screen.spec.json` (any NodeSpec JSON you or your agent write) to a document and export it as a Figma `.fig` file (container version 106).** `app.designos` is created if it does not exist: ```bash designos app.designos --apply-spec your-screen.spec.json designos app.designos --export-fig out.fig ``` `--export-fig` writes only to a path that ends in `.fig` and does not exist yet. Re-running it needs `--overwrite`, which replaces an existing regular file; a symbolic link is never written through. 3. **Render the file on the CPU and on the GPU, then compare the two PNGs.** `designos-diff` prints the SSIM score and exits `0` while the mismatch ratio stays under the threshold: ```bash designos-studio out.fig --size 1600x1000 --no-toast --screenshot cpu.png designos-studio out.fig --gpu --size 1600x1000 --no-toast --screenshot gpu.png designos-diff compare cpu.png gpu.png --tolerance 8 --threshold 0.02 --out diff.png ``` **The Practical Agentic Loop:** | Lifecycle Verb / Flag | Role in the Loop | | :--- | :--- | | **`--panel variables`** | Opens the Variables view: collections, modes and alias bindings. | | **`--panel agents`** | Opens the Agents panel: pick an agent CLI, resume the file's last session, or start from a sample prompt. | | **`--apply-spec / --export-fig`** | Compiles declarative JSON specs through Auto-Layout 5.0, then writes a `.fig` file (container version 106). | | **`--screenshot / designos-diff`** | Renders a headless frame, on the GPU with `--gpu`, and compares two PNGs. | ### 3. Ask in plain English (or invoke the Agent CLI directly) Open your project in your AI coding agent (or in the Studio's Agents panel) and describe the outcome you need: > "Apply `your-screen.spec.json` (any NodeSpec JSON you or your agent write) to a new document, export it to `out.fig`, and capture a 1600x1000 GPU screenshot." > "List the open comment threads, make the change each one asks for, and resolve the thread." > "Lint the open page with `designos_lint`, apply the safe fixes, and list what is left." > "Generate React, Tailwind and SwiftUI code for the selected frame, then compare a before and after screenshot with `designos-diff`." --- ## What's new Notes for every release are in the [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md). The newest is 0.7.17. The latest captures are from the 0.7.12 release build, and older releases are short lists. ### 0.7.17 - **Figma layout.** Instances keep the layout Figma stored for them, whichever page of a `.fig` file you open first. On the Untitled UI PRO v8.0 kit, the instances that refuse Figma's stored layout fall from 1,052 to 22, and opening is not slower (a median of 9.49 s against 9.92 s before). A real edit of a main still makes its instances refuse the stored layout, and saving a page you never opened keeps its stored layout. The 22 that remain sit inside mains that hold no stored record. - **Scaled text.** Text inside a scaled instance draws at Figma's size and keeps its text style: a 14/20 px style in a 0.8 instance draws at 11.2/16 px, as in Figma. On the kit, 1,727 scaled instances hold 931 text layers; texts whose font size is off from Figma's stored value fall from 104 to 0, pixel line heights from 104 to 0, and letter spacing from 581 to 4. Detaching a scaled instance, creating a component from it, or pasting a text out of it keeps the values the text is drawn with, and the inspector shows the size it is drawn at (11.2 / 16, not 14 / 20). The scaled-text fix was carried from a pull request by @NamAIEngineer. - **Missing fonts.** A text whose font is not installed draws the glyph outlines Figma saved in the `.fig` file instead of a substitute font: an icon font missing on this machine shows its icons instead of empty boxes, and a missing brand font keeps Figma's letter shapes and line breaks, on the CPU and GPU canvas and in PNG, SVG and PDF export. The saved outlines stay only while the text and its box match what Figma saved. Large files do not keep these outlines yet. By @NamAIEngineer. - **Export.** Export bounds count a layer's own box only when Figma does: a layer that is not a frame and paints nothing adds no box, and a frame always adds its full box. Float noise such as 100.0006 no longer adds a pixel, while 100.5 still rounds up. Two kit frames still differ from Figma: Dashboards 01 Desktop is 4 px too wide and Settings pages 02 Mobile 5 px too wide. - **Agents and editing.** An edit's layout belongs to its own undo step: when an agent (through `designos-mcp`) or a history command adds, removes or moves a layer, the auto-layout frames above it are solved and the groups that hold it are refitted in the same step, so one undo restores the edit and the layout together. Each live patch an agent sends carries that layout, so the open editor ends with the agent's document; a random parity test compares every node, and 2,000 rounds run clean. A session whose tab was closed now refuses every later edit with a final "tab closed" error and writes nothing. A connector picks its line and label ink from the surface it sits on, also over gradients, images, blend-mode fills and translucent fills. By @NamAIEngineer. - **Testing.** A new ignored test, the kit fidelity scoreboard, measures Studio feature by feature against the data Figma stored in the Untitled UI PRO v8.0 kit, with no Figma needed at run time. First results, measured before the instance-layout and scaled-text fixes above landed: auto-layout child placement 99.1%, hug frames' own size 99.4%, text layout 69.9%. ### 0.7.16 - **Lines and strokes.** A line you change in an imported Figma file is drawn where Figma draws it. A solid centred line with a butt or round cap sits as a band above its axis instead of half a stroke weight off, on the canvas, in SVG and PDF export, in export bounds and in click and hover hit testing. On 8,227 kit lines, the live drawing now differs from Figma's stored outline on 0 pixels, where the old drawing differed on 27,249,471. A stored stroke outline is drawn only while it still matches the layer's size and stroke. Square caps, arrow caps, dashed lines and Inside or Outside lines still draw centred, because Figma's placement for them is not measured yet. - **Export.** Export bounds follow what Figma measures. Each side of a stroke uses its own weight (outside adds the full weight on that side, centre half, inside nothing), and a frame's shadow also grows around its children: cut to the frame when it clips, and cast from the children alone when the frame has no fill. The SVG shadow region follows the same shapes. With every page loaded, 8 of the 10 kit frames checked are within 1 px of Figma; the other two are still 4 px and 5 px too wide. - **Figma files.** A `.fig` page that was never opened keeps more of what you edit: changing an instance's auto layout there (spacing 4 to 20, for example) is saved, where reopening used to bring back 4, and a new instance of a main that holds a nested instance from such a page shows that nested instance's layers at once. A main component sync with no change keeps instances where Figma stored them: layers moved off Figma's geometry on the Untitled UI PRO v8.0 kit drop from 119 to 40. Keys of a Figma REST JSON file that Studio does not model are kept on open, save, undo and export. A `.jam` (FigJam) file opens as a Board document, and a stroke outline Figma stored is no longer written back after the stroke weight was edited. - **Agents and saving.** An agent in a Studio tab can no longer widen its own designos tool list: after the first start, the list in force can only be narrowed. Saves from the command line refuse a symbolic link, a hard linked file and a wrong file ending, and an agent's save never writes through a symbolic link. On macOS an overwrite keeps the file's ACL, extended attributes and mode. - **Fixes.** The Overrides list of an instance shows the overrides parked on a layer the current variant lacks, each marked "(not in variant)" with its own Reset. A wrapped auto layout can keep its line gap following item spacing, as in Figma. Setting a variable or switching a variable mode in the prototype player re-resolves the variants bound to it. A text colour edit reaches every layer with text in the selection, sticky notes included. Editing one table cell on a 400 x 400 table takes 0.03 to 0.05 ms instead of 1.37 s. Many fixes were carried from pull requests by @NamAIEngineer. ### 0.7.15 - **Components.** A nested instance keeps its overrides when its variant is switched by hand and back, and an override on a layer the other variant lacks comes back when the instance is switched back. The switch report now gives two numbers: dropped, and kept for a return. Rows of a nested instance in the component panel show the variable pill and offer the same bind control as top-level rows. - **Figma files.** A `.fig` saved with pages that were never opened keeps more of what the user did: a duplicated page keeps its instances' child overrides, a reset field is dropped from the saved entry, a move is saved, and a variable binding is dropped only for the field that was edited. A variable collection marked not publishable stays that way through import and save, and stays out of the published assets and the design-system search. - **Lines and shapes.** An imported line resized through the agent tools or a variable-bound size keeps its stroke outline stretched as the editor does, and a dash array of `[0, 0]` counts as solid. A child with no fill area counts as an empty operand in a boolean operation. A hairline ring with an Inside or Outside stroke exports to SVG as one ellipse, as the canvas draws it. - **Agents.** An image job whose agent start is refused for good fails at once with the agent menu's sentence and one error toast, and so does every job queued behind it. The mode control shows the mode the next send uses, and a click on the mode menu, the attach menu or the @ popup reaches the row instead of the terminal under it. - **Fixes.** A plain click on a corner radius or shape handle changes nothing and leaves no undo step, a panic in the macOS quit callback no longer aborts the app, a toast with a button is always kept, and the rules pack lists more errors that `designos_apply_spec` can return. Many fixes were carried from pull requests by @NamAIEngineer. ### 0.7.14 - **Components.** A component property whose default is bound to a variable in Figma keeps that binding through `.fig` and Figma REST import, `.fig` export and the design-system scan. A value picked by hand for one variable-bound variant property holds only that property, and the others keep following their variables. A variant switch keeps a text override and the instance's size, and reports every override it has to drop. A frame that hugs an instance takes its new size in the same step as a variant switch that a variable drives, also when the instance sits inside a group. - **Agents.** The approval mode Ask for risky only is now called Ask when risky, and it is enforced for every way of starting an agent: a CLI that does not share the approval hook is refused with its reason and the next step. A running agent tab keeps the permission mode it was started in. - **Auto layout.** Older frames with auto spacing, and wrapped frames with room left on the counter axis, are placed as Figma places them. Re-solving every auto-layout frame of the imported Untitled UI PRO v8.0 kit moves 1,910 of 194,397 layers by more than 0.5 px; it was 2,039. - **Figma files.** Opening a page for the first time after its main component was edited shows the instances at the main's new size and keeps their overrides. A change made inside a nested component copy survives a `.fig` save, a reopen and an edit of the main component. - **Fixes.** Corner radius edits and bindings on imported shapes redraw, a large background blur at the edge of the canvas matches the CPU reference, a `.pen` export keeps an instance's own ring arc, and the agent tools refuse more clearly (`INSTANCE_CHILD`, `INSTANCE_CYCLE`, library variables are read-only). Many fixes were carried from pull requests by @NamAIEngineer. ### 0.7.13 - **Auto layout.** Rotated and flipped children are laid out by their visual bounding box, as in Figma: a 72 x 18 text turned 270 degrees takes 18 px of a row, not 72. A wrapped frame from a `.fig` import with no counter-axis gap uses its item spacing as the line gap, and a `.fig` frame with no right or bottom padding imports it as 0. Re-solving every auto-layout frame of the imported Untitled UI PRO v8.0 kit moved 61,948 of 194,397 layers by more than 0.5 px before this release and moves 2,039 now. - **Components.** A nested instance whose variant is bound to a variable follows the mode where it sits: a mode set on the host frame, an ancestor, the wrapper instance or the page. An instance keeps its own ring arc (start, sweep, inner radius) when its main component's arc changes, and Reset gives the main's arc back. - **`.fig` save.** A save keeps the overrides of an instance on a page that was never opened after its main component is edited. A vector resized inside an instance keeps its size through a save and reopen; that already held, and tests now pin it. - **Export and canvas.** Dashed, gradient and width-bound Inside strokes on a grid that are wider than the padding export as an inset shadow, so content no longer shifts. SwiftUI export splits unequal grid columns such as 2fr 1fr by their weights (iOS 16 or macOS 13). The grid overlay draws its gap bands in the real gaps. - **Fixes.** A refused edit, such as an instance swap that would make a component contain itself, shows a toast that says why, and a Display P3 document caps its converted-image cache at 64 MiB. Several fixes were carried from pull requests by @NamAIEngineer. ### 0.7.12 Captured with the 0.7.12 release build, headlessly with `designos-studio --screenshot` (2x), on a copy of the Untitled UI PRO v8.0 Figma kit, by Untitled UI. Click the image for full size. The page is the kit's Dropdowns page of the copy, and `--panel effect-glass` adds a default glass effect to the selected Menu layer for the capture.

Glass popover
Light angle, light intensity, refraction, depth, dispersion and frost each get a bind button, so a number variable can drive them.
Command: designos-studio dropdowns.designos --select id:27478 --panel effect-glass --zoom 100 --size 1440x900 --scale 2 --no-toast --screenshot docs/images/v0.7.12/glass-variable-slots.png
- **Variables on effects.** Blur radius, spread, offset and opacity of an effect, and the glass settings, bind to number variables. They resolve per mode, survive `.fig` and work from MCP. - **Size limits and type.** Min and max width and height bind to number variables and feed auto layout. Font family, font style, paragraph spacing and paragraph indent bind on text layers. - **Motion.** Easing and duration variables bind to prototype transitions and Motion tracks, and Motion timelines import from and export to `.fig`. - **Animation styles.** A style holds Motion timelines, layers link to it like effect and grid styles, and the style picker lists it. - **Extended collections.** Publish an extended collection to a library and use it from another file, with edits in the receiving file's own modes. - **Fixes.** Editing a shared text style keeps the properties a linked layer overrides, and a branch merge keeps extensions pointing at the right parent. Several fixes were carried from pull requests by @NamAIEngineer. ### 0.7.11 - **Tables.** A document can hold a table that you edit on the canvas: type in a cell, Tab between cells, drag a line to resize, merge and unmerge from the right-click menu. Agents build tables with the `table` op of `designos_apply_batch`. - **Colour.** Set a document to Display P3 from the Page title row, and pick one Colour format export setting (Hex, RGB or OKLCH) for CSS, Tailwind, React, HTML and Dev Mode. - **Extended collections.** A variable collection can extend a parent and override its variables per mode, as in Figma, through the panel, `.fig`, Figma REST JSON and MCP. - **Instance properties.** Bind boolean, text and variant properties of an instance to variables, and keep your overrides when you swap an instance or switch its variant. - **Text styles.** A text layer keeps its style when you change weight, italic or underline, shows a count pill, and "Reapply style" restores the style in one undo step. - **`.fig` save.** A save keeps the overrides of instances nested inside a main component, including pages that were never opened. ### 0.7.10 - **Save keeps every page.** A save of a large `.fig` no longer drops the content of pages that were never opened. Files imported before this fix: import them again from the original `.fig`. - **Connectors.** Draw a live connector with the Connector tool (X). It sticks to two layers and re-routes when one moves. Agents draw one with the `connect` op of `designos_apply_batch`. - **`.fig` save.** A save keeps every variable the file uses, deleted ones included, and writes instance fill and stroke overrides as the file recorded them. - **Saving takes longer.** A large `.fig` loads every page first, so Save As on the Untitled UI kit went from 6.6 s to 38.2 s. - **App and security.** Quitting from the Dock asks "Save changes?" when a tab has unsaved edits, and private approval folders with an extended ACL are refused. - **Fixes.** Nested Stretch instances keep their size, a component can no longer hold an instance of itself, and background blur behind a translucent child of a paintless group blurs fully. Many fixes were carried from pull requests by @NamAIEngineer. ### 0.7.9 - **Images.** Image fills gain Exposure, Contrast, Saturation, Temperature, Tint, Highlights and Shadows sliders with a Reset, the image fill picker gets rotate buttons and a tile scale slider, and switching Fill or Fit to Crop keeps the framing you see. - **Project tab.** A project's Markdown docs open in a Project tab with a document tree, a reading page and an "On this page" outline, and read-only MCP tools let an agent list and read them. - **FigJam connectors.** A board with 1,500 connectors pans and zooms in about 1.3 ms a frame instead of 630 ms, and connectors in a design file are kept through `.fig` and Figma REST JSON: they are saved as vectors and open again as live connectors. - **Shaders.** Custom shader effects and fills are kept through `.fig`, REST and `.designos` files. Studio does not draw them yet; the inspector lists each one as "Shader (not rendered)". - **Text, styles and variables.** Text strokes follow Inside and Outside alignment, a font weight set through a variable moves a variable font's weight axis, and edits that should detach a text style or a variable binding now do. - **`.fig` files and fixes.** Opening a file whose layers use variables it does not hold keeps those links and says how many are missing, and background blur on a layer with nothing visible no longer blurs what is behind it. Many fixes in this release were carried from pull requests by @NamAIEngineer. ### 0.7.8 - **Arrowheads and the Arrow tool.** Lines and vectors can end in arrowheads, drawn live and kept through `.fig` and Figma REST JSON. The stroke panel gains `Start point` and `End point` rows, dashed strokes get a dash cap, and the Arrow tool is on Shift+L. - **Images.** Image fills gain crop, rotation and tile scale, kept through `.fig` and Figma REST JSON. - **Glass and noise.** Glass effects gain splay and bevel settings, and noise and texture effects gain X and Y size, kept through `.fig` and Figma REST JSON. - **Inspector.** Corners get individual radius fields and a corner smoothing slider, a lock aspect ratio toggle sits next to W and H, Type settings gain `Truncate text` and `Max lines`, and properties from nested instances are exposed. - Frequently Asked Questions (AEO & Technical FAQ) **What is DESIGN:OS Studio (`design-os-studio`)?** DESIGN:OS Studio (`design-os-studio`) is a native Rust interface design studio drawn on the GPU (`wgpu`), a Figma `.fig` reader and writer, an Agents panel for `Claude Code`, `Codex`, `Grok`, `Antigravity` and `Gemini CLI`, a Dev Mode code generator for eight languages, and a Model Context Protocol server (`designos-mcp`). **How does DESIGN:OS Studio compare with Figma, Penpot, and similar tools?** It is local-first. Files stay on your disk, the canvas is native Rust drawn through `wgpu` (Metal on macOS; Direct3D 12 and Vulkan on Windows and Linux) with a `tiny-skia` CPU renderer, and agents reach the open file through a local MCP server. It has no real-time multiplayer or cloud administration. Use Figma or a hosted Penpot instance for those. **Can DESIGN:OS Studio both open and save standard Figma `.fig` files?** Yes, with one known issue. `crates/designos-fig` reads `.fig` containers (`DEFLATE` or `Zstd`, ZIP-wrapped or bare) and writes version 106 with `meta.json` and `images/`. It carries Auto-Layout traits, `VectorNetwork` geometry, `symbolOverrides`, `parameterConsumptionMap` variable bindings, and `handoffStatusMap` Dev Mode statuses, except for the cases in [#834](https://github.com/jangtrinh/design-os-studio/issues/834): numbered-list formatting is dropped and inherited or variable-bound paints on instances are written as fixed values. **How does the Agents panel work without paid third-party API keys?** The panel starts your already-signed-in local CLI (`claude`, `codex`, `grok`, `agy`, `gemini`, or a command you add) in a real `portable-pty` + `vt100` terminal tab. Studio sets `DESIGNOS_BIN`, `DESIGNOS_FILE`, and `DESIGNOS_SESSION_DIR` for the session and registers `designos-mcp` with the CLIs that support it, and the composer sends into the live session. Each CLI bills through its own plan, not through Studio. **How fast does DESIGN:OS Studio render large files?** It limits work to the viewport with a spatial index of 2048-unit grid cells (`SceneIndex`) and zoom-based level of detail, shares meshes between repeated shapes (`GeomCache`), and reuses the cached frame when nothing changed (`FrameKey`). On Metal, an idle view used 0.01 s of CPU in 20 s on the 336 MB Untitled UI PRO kit, which has 207,601 nodes, measured with v0.6.0 on an Apple M4 Max. Load time depends on the file and the machine. **How is DESIGN:OS Studio installed and licensed?** Pre-built packages are available for macOS (`.dmg` + `.tar.gz`, verified on Apple Silicon), Windows (`.zip` with a per-user `install.ps1`), and Linux (`.deb` + `.tar.gz`). The Windows and Linux packages are built by the same release workflow but are not verified before release. Or you can build from source with `cargo run --release -p designos-app --bin designos-studio`. It is source-available under PolyForm Shield 1.0.0, with no telemetry.

Why this exists

Why DESIGN:OS Studio?

Browser-based design tools keep your files on a vendor's servers and give coding agents little more than a REST export. design-os-studio is a local-first studio written in Rust. It reads and writes .fig files on your disk, runs your own agent CLI in an Agents panel, and serves the open file to agents through a local MCP server.

| Dimension | DESIGN:OS Studio | How to check |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| Rendering | Native Rust canvas: wgpu on Metal, DirectX 12 or Vulkan, with a tiny-skia CPU renderer for headless captures. It requests no repaint while the view is idle (FrameKey frame reuse). | Open a file, leave it still, and read the process CPU time twice with ps -o time= -p <pid>. |

| Large files | A spatial index of 2048-unit grid cells (SceneIndex) limits work to the viewport, and repeated shapes share one mesh (GeomCache). The 336 MB Untitled UI PRO kit opens as one document of 207,601 nodes. | designos <file> --inspect-json prints the node count. |

| .fig files | Reads .fig containers (fig-kiwi, DEFLATE or Zstd) and writes container version 106, in a ZIP with meta.json and images/. Known issue in 0.6.0: saving a .fig drops numbered-list formatting and writes inherited or variable-bound paints on instances as fixed values. | Export a file, then read the version from the canvas.fig header (see below). |

| Agents | The Agents panel starts your own agent CLI (Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Antigravity or Gemini CLI) as a live session on the open file, and keeps a file's sessions across restarts. Each CLI uses its own sign-in, so Studio needs no API key. | designos-studio <file> --panel agents |

| MCP server | designos-mcp serves its tools over stdio: see the design, read its design system, write in one step (designos_apply_batch) and lint the result (designos_lint). | Send tools/list to designos-mcp --workspace <dir>. The tool table below is generated from that list. |

| Variables | Color, number, string and boolean variables in collections with modes. A frame can pin its own mode per collection, and modes round-trip through .fig. Import and export Figma JSON and W3C Design Tokens (DTCG). | designos <file> --export-variables <out> |

| Dev Mode | Built-in Dev Mode (Shift+D) with code in CSS, Tailwind, React, SwiftUI, UIKit, Compose, Android XML and HTML. | designos <file> --select <layer> --codegen react |

| Privacy and license | No telemetry. Studio makes these network requests: open-licensed font downloads from the Fontsource API when a file uses fonts you do not have, a public status-page check after an agent provider error, a connection check when you click Retry connection, and a plugin download from GitHub when you install a plugin. The agent CLIs you start use the network under their own terms. Source-available under PolyForm Shield 1.0.0. | git grep -n 'ureq::' -- crates lists the HTTP calls. The Figma REST client in designos-fig is a cargo feature that is off by default. |

To read the container version of an exported file, run unzip -p out.fig canvas.fig | head -c 12 | xxd. The header starts with fig-kiwi and ends with 6a00 0000, which is 106 in little-endian.

> Where hosted tools win, and it is not close: real-time multiplayer with live cursors, enterprise cloud administration with SSO and SCIM, and hosted comment notifications by email or Slack. Studio has none of these. If your workflow needs real-time cloud multiplayer without local file ownership, use Figma (paired with our live bridge design-os-figma-plugin) or a hosted Penpot instance instead.

Quickstart

1. Install once

Install the agent skill plugin in Claude Code, copy the skill into Codex, download a release package (.dmg, .zip, .deb, .tar.gz), or build the four binaries from source:


# Option A: Claude Code plugin marketplace

/plugin marketplace add jangtrinh/design-os-studio

/plugin install design-os-studio@design-os-studio



# Option B: Clone and launch the native Rust/wgpu Studio (or package a .dmg / .zip / .deb)

git clone https://github.com/jangtrinh/design-os-studio

cd design-os-studio

cargo run --release -p designos-app --bin designos-studio

./scripts/build-release.sh <version> --local-host

<a id="first-safe-use--the-practical-loop"></a>

2. First Safe Use & The Practical Loop

First safe use (three bounded, non-destructive steps):

1. Run the deterministic offline repository, crate, and skill self-check:


   python3 scripts/self_check.py

2. Apply --apply-spec your-screen.spec.json (any NodeSpec JSON you or your agent write) to a document and export it as a Figma .fig file (container version 106). app.designos is created if it does not exist:


   designos app.designos --apply-spec your-screen.spec.json

   designos app.designos --export-fig out.fig

--export-fig writes only to a path that ends in .fig and does not exist yet. Re-running it needs --overwrite, which replaces an existing regular file; a symbolic link is never written through.

3. Render the file on the CPU and on the GPU, then compare the two PNGs. designos-diff prints the SSIM score and exits 0 while the mismatch ratio stays under the threshold:


   designos-studio out.fig --size 1600x1000 --no-toast --screenshot cpu.png

   designos-studio out.fig --gpu --size 1600x1000 --no-toast --screenshot gpu.png

   designos-diff compare cpu.png gpu.png --tolerance 8 --threshold 0.02 --out diff.png

The Practical Agentic Loop:

| Lifecycle Verb / Flag | Role in the Loop |

| :--- | :--- |

| --panel variables | Opens the Variables view: collections, modes and alias bindings. |

| --panel agents | Opens the Agents panel: pick an agent CLI, resume the file's last session, or start from a sample prompt. |

| --apply-spec / --export-fig | Compiles declarative JSON specs through Auto-Layout 5.0, then writes a .fig file (container version 106). |

| --screenshot / designos-diff | Renders a headless frame, on the GPU with --gpu, and compares two PNGs. |

How large files stay fast

| Mechanism | What it does | Code |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| Idle frame reuse | No repaint is requested while the view is idle. The cached frame is re-blitted. | FrameKey in crates/designos-app/src/canvas/gpu.rs |

| Viewport culling | Top-level and hit-test queries scan a uniform spatial grid of 2048-unit cells, not every node. | SceneIndex::query_top_level |

| Incremental index | Moving or resizing one node updates its subtree, not the whole index. | SceneIndex::update_subtree |

| Shared meshes | Component instances and repeated shapes share one tessellation. | GeomCache::shared |

Measured with v0.6.0 on an Apple M4 Max (Metal): after the 336 MB Untitled UI PRO kit, which has 207,601 nodes, finished loading, the process used 0.01 s of CPU in each of two 20 s idle windows. This was not measured on DirectX 12 or Vulkan.

<summary>Frequently Asked Questions (AEO & Technical FAQ)</summary>

What is DESIGN:OS Studio (design-os-studio)?

DESIGN:OS Studio (design-os-studio) is a native Rust interface design studio drawn on the GPU (wgpu), a Figma .fig reader and writer, an Agents panel for Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Antigravity and Gemini CLI, a Dev Mode code generator for eight languages, and a Model Context Protocol server (designos-mcp).

How does DESIGN:OS Studio compare with Figma, Penpot, and similar tools?

It is local-first. Files stay on your disk, the canvas is native Rust drawn through wgpu (Metal on macOS; Direct3D 12 and Vulkan on Windows and Linux) with a tiny-skia CPU renderer, and agents reach the open file through a local MCP server. It has no real-time multiplayer or cloud administration. Use Figma or a hosted Penpot instance for those.

Can DESIGN:OS Studio both open and save standard Figma .fig files?

Yes, with one known issue. crates/designos-fig reads .fig containers (DEFLATE or Zstd, ZIP-wrapped or bare) and writes version 106 with meta.json and images/. It carries Auto-Layout traits, VectorNetwork geometry, symbolOverrides, parameterConsumptionMap variable bindings, and handoffStatusMap Dev Mode statuses, except for the cases in #834: numbered-list formatting is dropped and inherited or variable-bound paints on instances are written as fixed values.

How does the Agents panel work without paid third-party API keys?

The panel starts your already-signed-in local CLI (claude, codex, grok, agy, gemini, or a command you add) in a real portable-pty + vt100 terminal tab. Studio sets DESIGNOS_BIN, DESIGNOS_FILE, and DESIGNOS_SESSION_DIR for the session and registers designos-mcp with the CLIs that support it, and the composer sends into the live session. Each CLI bills through its own plan, not through Studio.

How fast does DESIGN:OS Studio render large files?

It limits work to the viewport with a spatial index of 2048-unit grid cells (SceneIndex) and zoom-based level of detail, shares meshes between repeated shapes (GeomCache), and reuses the cached frame when nothing changed (FrameKey). On Metal, an idle view used 0.01 s of CPU in 20 s on the 336 MB Untitled UI PRO kit, which has 207,601 nodes, measured with v0.6.0 on an Apple M4 Max. Load time depends on the file and the machine.

How is DESIGN:OS Studio installed and licensed?

Pre-built packages are available for macOS (.dmg + .tar.gz, verified on Apple Silicon), Windows (.zip with a per-user install.ps1), and Linux (.deb + .tar.gz). The Windows and Linux packages are built by the same release workflow but are not verified before release. Or you can build from source with cargo run --release -p designos-app --bin designos-studio. It is source-available under PolyForm Shield 1.0.0, with no telemetry.
